display.title: The Cradle: The Alter Rebbe Hears a Baby's Cry
display.summary_short: Deep in learning, the Mitteler Rebbe does not hear his baby fall from the crib. The Alter Rebbe comes downstairs, comforts the child and teaches that we must always hear a child's cry.
display.summary_long: The Alter Rebbe lived upstairs, and his son Reb DovBer, later the Mitteler Rebbe, lived downstairs with his family. The Mitteler Rebbe learned Torah with such concentration that he heard nothing around him. One day the Alter Rebbe, learning upstairs, heard a baby crying. He closed his sefer, kissed it, and went down to find his little grandchild lying on the floor beside the crib while the Mitteler Rebbe learned on, unaware. The Alter Rebbe lovingly picked up the baby, held it until it calmed down, and rocked it back to sleep. Later he told his son that one must never be so busy with learning or serving Hashem that he does not hear the cry of a child. The Rebbe often repeated this story. The storyteller applies it to us: our own learning and mitzvos are not enough; we must notice the needs of siblings, friends and neighbors, and of every Jew whose soul is crying to learn Torah and do mitzvos, and carry something along, like tefillin or Shabbos candles, to give someone the chance to do a mitzvah.
display.lesson: Never be so busy, even with learning or serving Hashem, that you do not hear the cry of a child or the needs of another Jew.

sources_cited.note: The Rebbe often repeated this story and its lesson.

quality.notes: Spoken in English despite the Hebrew filename (arisah = cradle).
